summary: Remove the companion MCP server entirely: delete cmd/canvas-pp-mcp and internal/mcp, drop the build/install Makefile targets, drop the canvas-pp-mcp goreleaser build and its Homebrew install line, and strip MCP setup from README/SKILL/AGENTS/CLAUDE. A reprint must not reintroduce it.
reason:
Removed at the maintainer's direction, on Canvas Terms of Service grounds. This record exists so a reprint does not silently restore the server; the decision is a product constraint, not a defect in the generated code.

One thing a future reader should understand about the scope of this patch, because it is easy to over-read: removing the MCP server does not change a single Canvas API call. Every MCP tool was a shell-out to the sibling canvas-pp-cli binary (internal/mcp/cobratree/shellout.go), using the same bearer token against the same endpoints. Request traffic reaching Canvas was byte-identical whether it originated from the CLI or from an MCP host. What the removal does change is which processes can reach Canvas data: the server was the path that put a user's Canvas token and responses in front of shell-less hosted chat apps (Claude Desktop over stdio, ChatGPT Desktop over -transport http on a local port with no authentication of its own). If a future maintainer is relying on this patch for a compliance property, that egress-surface reduction is the property it actually delivers. Any constraint on what the CLI itself may do with the API is not addressed here and needs its own control.

The server was already documented as optional and redundant for shell-capable agents -- README and SKILL both told terminal-having agents to skip it -- so removal costs nothing for the primary integration path (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Cursor, Aider). It does drop a previously released binary: users who installed canvas-pp-mcp from a prior release or the Homebrew tap will not receive it on the next release, and the Homebrew formula no longer installs it. Hosts with no shell are now explicitly unsupported rather than quietly broken, and README says so.

Upstream: CLI Printing Press generates the MCP server as a standard companion for every printed CLI. Suppressing it per-CLI belongs in the generator's print configuration rather than in a post-print deletion; until that exists, this record is the reprint guard.
known_limitations:
The generated command tree still carries the codegen annotations the MCP walker consumed: `mcp:read-only` in 641 files under internal/cli/ and one `mcp:hidden` in internal/cli/search.go. They are inert Cobra Annotations map entries -- nothing reads them now that internal/mcp/cobratree is gone -- and they were deliberately left in place. Stripping them would mean editing 641 generated files, which is exactly the kind of wide hand-edit to generated output that AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md warn against, and it would create a large reprint conflict surface for zero runtime effect. If the generator later stops emitting them, nothing here needs to change. A comment in internal/cliutil/verifyenv.go also still refers to `mcp:read-only` as the marker that classifies mutating operations; that reference describes the codegen marker, which still exists, so it remains accurate.

This patch removes a transport, not a capability. Anyone with a shell can still do everything through canvas-pp-cli, with the same token and the same reach.

One earlier patch record, version-from-build-info.json, lists cmd/canvas-pp-mcp/main.go among the files it touched. That record is left unedited: it is an accurate account of what that change did at the time, and rewriting it to match the current tree would falsify the ledger. A reprint applier working through the records in order should treat that one file target as obsolete -- this record supersedes it.
validated_outcome:
cmd/canvas-pp-mcp and internal/mcp are deleted; `grep -rn 'canvas-pp-cli/internal/mcp'` returns nothing, confirming the only importer went with them. `go mod tidy` dropped mark3labs/mcp-go from both go.mod and go.sum. `go build ./...` succeeds and `go test ./...` passes 6 packages (cli, client, cliutil, config, store, plus cmd with no test files) -- previously 7, the removed one being internal/mcp. No non-MCP test was touched.

Build config: .goreleaser.yaml has no canvas-pp-mcp build id and the brew formula installs only canvas-pp-cli; Makefile has no build-mcp/install-mcp/build-all, and the now-dead `make build-all` reference was removed from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md to match. Docs: README's 'Use with chat apps that can't run commands' section is replaced with an explicit unsupported note, and no install instruction, config snippet, or path-relocation example references the server. The only surviving 'canvas-pp-mcp' string in README is in the third-party related-projects list, where it names an unrelated project by another author.
